source_of_truth: This file. The rule exists only on the clients (#410/#411); the iOS reference is CloudSession.removalCompletesLocally, the tolerance is CloudSession.clockSkewTolerance.
description: 'Remove this device' sends a revoke. When the revoke FAILS, the client finishes removal locally (drops the credential) iff the status is 401 or 404 AND the response Date header is present, parses as an RFC 9110 IMF-fixdate, and is within clock_skew_tolerance_seconds of the device clock (inclusive). Everything else keeps the credential: other statuses (429, 503, any 5xx, 403, 400, 410), no response (status null), and a Date that is missing, empty, unparseable, in an obsolete format, or skewed. Evaluate each case with the device clock at now_epoch; date_header_raw is the header exactly as received (null when absent), and date_offset_seconds is what it encodes relative to now_epoch (null when it encodes nothing usable).

cases.name: 404-in-sync
cases.why: The server forgot the credential and the clocks agree.

cases.name: 401-in-sync
cases.why: 401 and 404 are indistinguishable by design.

cases.name: 404-ahead-at-tolerance
cases.why: Exactly at +tolerance: inclusive.

cases.name: 404-behind-at-tolerance
cases.why: Exactly at -tolerance: inclusive.

cases.name: 404-ahead-past-tolerance
cases.why: One second past: the device clock may be the reason.

cases.name: 404-behind-past-tolerance
cases.why: One second past, the other way.

cases.name: 401-ahead-at-tolerance
cases.why: The boundary holds for 401 too.

cases.name: 401-behind-past-tolerance
cases.why: And so does the refusal past it.

cases.name: 404-badly-skewed
cases.why: An hour off: every signed request would be refused anyway.

cases.name: 404-no-date
cases.why: No Date header: skew cannot be ruled out, so keep.

cases.name: 401-no-date
cases.why: Same for 401.

cases.name: 404-empty-date
cases.why: An empty header is an absent one.

cases.name: 404-garbage-date
cases.why: Unparseable is absent.

cases.name: 404-rfc850-date
cases.why: The obsolete RFC 850 form is not parsed, so it counts as absent.

cases.name: 404-asctime-date
cases.why: Nor is asctime.

cases.name: 429-in-sync
cases.why: Rate limited: transient, keep the credential.

cases.name: 503-in-sync
cases.why: Unavailable: transient.

cases.name: 500-in-sync
cases.why: Server error: unexplained.

cases.name: 502-in-sync
cases.why: Bad gateway: transient.

cases.name: 403-in-sync
cases.why: Only 401 and 404 mean 'no such credential'.

cases.name: 400-in-sync
cases.why: Malformed request: our bug, not the server forgetting us.

cases.name: 410-in-sync
cases.why: Not one of the two statuses, however suggestive.

cases.name: offline
cases.why: No response at all: keep the credential.
